text:
alex_k: Quick FYI — seeing slow but steady GPU memory growth on a small subset of Qwen-MQA hosts after long-context streaming tests. Not the usual fragmentation spike, looks like some pages are being held after big batch bursts.

maria_g: I noticed this yesterday during the dialog stress runs. It only happens when we have an initial "priming" batch (batch_size >= 12) with long prefix (~1k tokens) followed by many single-token streams.

samir: any perf traces or heap maps?

alex_k: Attached a short extract from perfbot below. Repro steps included. Logs are from host qwen-mqa-34.

perfbot: profiling snapshot attached

perfbot: ```
# perf summary (kv manager)
alloc_pages_total: 16384
allocated_segments: 421
pinned_pages: 1276
evictable_pages: 18
last_evict_scan: 168ms ago
eviction_hysteresis_ms: 30000
avg_page_reuse_interval_ms: 12200
hot_page_ratio: 0.62
# observed during run: initial burst (priming) then long tail of single-token streams
```

tasha: That eviction_hysteresis_ms looks suspicious — 30s. Means pages marked recently-used aren't considered for eviction for a long time, so priming can pin many pages.

maria_g: Exactly. On Qwen-MQA the per-token KV stride is larger (multi-query layout), so priming touches more pages per sequence length compared to Llama. With rope scaling enabled the effective seq-length mapping shifts which increases page coverage.

samir: Do we have a kernel selection angle? i.e., a different attention kernel causing more KV writes that don't get compacted?

alex_k: We observed the MQA layout uses a separate layout kernel path that writes interleaved KV blocks. The compaction sweep expects contiguous ranges and misses many small, scattered free ranges. So reused pages are not coalesced.

maria_g: Repro script (short):

perfbot: ```bash
# reproduce on single host
./bench_stream --model qwen-mqa-7b --priming_batch 16 --priming_prefix 1024 \
  --streams 1200 --stream_batch 1 --rope_scale auto --collect-trace=/tmp/trace.pb
```

tasha: Quick mitigations we tried:
- reduce priming_batch to <=8 -> immediate drop in pinned_pages
- lower eviction_hysteresis to 5s -> reclaim within 10s
- run background compaction pass every 60s that looks for small free segments and merges them

samir: Can we automate priming-aware unwinding? Idea: when we detect a large priming burst, mark pages as "eligible-after-N-calls" instead of time-based hysteresis. That gives us a call-count based de-pinning.

alex_k: Nice. Could also bias routing: send priming-heavy requests to hosts flagged as "priming-safe" with extra headroom.

maria_g: Also, Qwen-MQA + rope_scale:auto seems to expand effective slot count by ~1.6x for long prefixes, so we should tune quantization of page indexes in the MQA kernel to prefer denser allocation.

perfbot: perf counters during mitigations:

perfbot: ```
# before mitigation
pinned_pages: 1276
mem_growth_per_1k_streams: 84MB
# after mitigation (priming_batch=8, hysteresis=5s)
pinned_pages: 312
mem_growth_per_1k_streams: 12MB
```

tasha: Action items:
- samir: prototype call-count de-pinning (ETA 2d)
- maria_g: add a compaction pass hook in runtime (ETA 3d)
- alex_k: add a routing flag and update e2e stress test to include priming-heavy scenario (ETA 1d)
- ops: consider rolling hysteresis config change as a temporary fix

maria_g: Logging note — let's add a small metric: priming_burst_size per minute and priming_pinned_pages to make alerting easier.

samir: I'll start an experimental branch: runtime/kv/depin-count and share a patch shortly.

alex_k: thanks all. once samir posts PR i'll run the 48h long-context run and report back. :thumbsup:
